end.summary:
Defined food miles as the kilometres food travels from where it is grown to where it is eaten.
Distinguished local and far-away food using spinach, apples, bananas, and Alphonso mangoes.
Connected longer journeys with more fuel use, pollution, and possible spoilage.
Suggested choosing food from nearer places to reduce food miles; noted that distance does not add nutrients.
Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Rohan practised identifying where food is grown, where it is eaten, and calculating the idea of food miles. They used the spinach example to explain why a 10-kilometre journey uses less fuel than a 1,500-kilometre journey. The idea that far-away food might be “special” was revisited with the point that distance does not add nutrients. At home, ask Rohan to trace one food from its growing place to the plate and discuss one limit of choosing local food.
